'''Cancelled expansions''' are Star Wars CCG sets Decipher announced after [[Death Star II]] and never published. CardGuide lists five of them as items 33–37, immediately after Theed Palace in the product order used on this wiki.<ref>https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_CCG</ref>

Decipher's own preview, ''After Death Star II'', said the classic trilogy on cards would keep growing after Death Star II as character-themed expansions rather than a straight walk through the films.<ref name="after">https://web.archive.org/web/20050307015419/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html</ref> The Death Star II Starter Deck rulebook carried a full-page ad for the first two of those sets.

== Death Star II starter ad ==

[[File:SoTE-Skywalkers-Ad-DSII-Starter-Deck.webp|400px|Advertisement printed in the Death Star II Starter Deck rulebook (© 2000 Decipher Inc.)]]

The Star Wars Customizable Card Game continues with '''''Shadows of the Empire''''' and '''''Skywalkers''''', the next two expansion sets, coming soon!

<blockquote>
'''Shadows of the Empire''' includes exciting new cards from the best-selling novel. Prince Xizor and Dash Rendar will be featured, along with their starships and a host of other characters and images in stunning photo-realistic detail!

'''Skywalkers''' will be the next full expansion in the Star Wars CCG. Not tied to the timeline of the film trilogy, it will be free to explore many aspects of the entire ''Star Wars'' universe. Many cards and themes will concentrate on Luke, Leia and… of course… Darth Vader.
</blockquote>

The page is copyright 2000 Decipher Inc., Norfolk, Virginia, used under Lucasfilm authorization.

== What shipped instead ==

Lucasfilm asked Decipher to mix ''The Phantom Menace'' into the original-trilogy game. [[Tatooine]] (May 2001) was originally framed as a Skywalker-family set and was rebuilt around podracing and Episode I characters.<ref>https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Tatooine_(expansion)</ref> [[Coruscant]], [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]], and [[Theed Palace]] followed; Theed Palace (12 December 2001) was the last Decipher expansion.

Encyclopedia 3.2 also records a Light Side [[Mara Jade]] photograph (green suit, same shoot as the Dark Side Enhanced Jabba's Palace card) that never became a retail card, plus planned extra language editions and anime-style Japanese cards that never shipped. Card leftovers are on [[Unreleased cards]]. Language editions, including the cancelled Spanish release, are on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. The Spanish Two-Player rules booklet from that program is on [[Spanish Premiere Two-Player Game rules booklet]].<ref name="encyc" />

Do not use the booster-pack mock-ups at the top of Encyclopedia 3.2 pages 201–202 as product photography; those packs were never sold.

The Players Committee later published virtual cards, beginning in 2002. Those sets are listed on the [[Main Page]] under Virtual Legacy (2002–2014) and current virtual sets (2014 Reset onward). They are not these cancelled Decipher expansions.
